#3087. Dutch Bros vs. Wendy's: Which Stock Is a Better Buy?

Dutch Bros is adding drive-thru shops at a rapid clip, while Wendy's relies on a franchise model built for steady cash flow. Their valuations tell very different stories.

Both Dutch Bros (BROS +6.50%) and Wendy's (WEN +1.22%) are different types of restaurant stocks, but each has the same challenge of creating more shareholder value. Dutch Bros is trying to build its future, while Wendy's is trying to improve its present.

Dutch Bros focuses on high-speed beverage service with a loyal following, while Wendy's leans on a massive global franchise network to deliver consistent results. Both compete for consumer dollars in a crowded market, but they offer very different risk and reward profiles for long-term investors.

Dutch Bros operates a rapidly growing network of drive-thru shops specializing in coffee, teas, and customizable energy drinks. In the competitive world of retail stocks, it relies on a unique culture and digital rewards to drive loyalty, particularly among younger consumers. The company sources its proprietary Rebel energy drinks through third-party partners.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $1.6 billion, representing a significant increase of approximately 27.9% over the prior year. This growth is largely driven by the opening of new locations across the United States. The company also reported net income of roughly $117.3 million, showing a substantial rise from the previous fiscal period.

Wendy's operates a global quick-service restaurant system with over 7,000 locations. The business uses a system optimization strategy involving buying and selling restaurant units to maintain an efficient mix of company-owned and franchised stores.

In FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $2.2 billion, which was a decrease of roughly 3.1% compared to the previous year. Despite the lower top-line figure, the company produced net income of nearly $165.1 million. This resulted in a net margin of close to 7.6%, a figure showing how much of every dollar in revenue becomes profit after all expenses.

Dutch Bros faces risks from its geographic concentration in the Western United States, making it vulnerable to regional economic shifts. The business also relies on a small group of suppliers for key ingredients, which could lead to disruptions if those partners fail to deliver. Additionally, rapid store expansion requires flawless execution, and any failure to manage this growth could harm the brand reputation.

Wendy's operates in the fiercely competitive quick-service industry against other major chains and convenience outlets. The company carries significant leverage through its securitized financing facility, which requires consistent cash flow to service. It also depends heavily on independent franchisees to maintain standards, as any food safety incident can damage the global brand.

Wendy's has a lower forward price-to-earnings (P/E) using future earnings estimates; Dutch Bros carries a higher price-to-sales (P/S) ratio measuring market cap against sales over the past twelve months.

When comparing two stocks, it really comes down to which one will create more value for a shareholder, and each of these stocks has its own set of risks and rewards.

The risks and rewards with Dutch Bros largely come down to its expansion plans. It's opening new locations rapidly, opening 48 stores in the third quarter of 2026, bringing it to over 1,200 locations. It hopes to reach over 2,000 stores by 2029. But it's not in every state, which limits its brand recognition. In its third quarter, it also shared that as a percentage of company-operated shops revenues, occupancy costs increased by 100 basis points, as the company shifted more of its portfolio to build-to-suit leases. Higher utility and other operating expenses also played a role. That's worth paying attention to because higher rent and utility costs could weigh on the profitability of new locations compared to some of its legacy locations. That means, while expansion is one of the biggest opportunities for the company, that expansion could also be one of the biggest risks, as new locations may cost more to open and operate and be less successful than legacy locations.

For Wendy's, it's a company that's already shown its potential, but it's at a stage where it's largely focused on improving what it's built. For the first nine months of 2026, net income is down 49.2%. Still, there's promise in its breakfast offerings, which management says could unlock "up to $200 million in restaurant-level EBITDA across the system." In addition, while shareholders wait for the turnaround to take shape, Wendy's pays a dividend that yields a generous 3.4%.

Choosing between these two boils down to believing in Dutch Bros' growth plan or the improvement plan of Wendy's.

#3086. After Jensen Huang, Big Tech Has a Chance to Learn From Nvidia’s Mistakes

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech insiders and commentators say Nvidia will survive Huang's departure, but it's time for more accountability among CEOs.

What now for Nvidia? This was the question on everyone’s lips at the illustrious Web Summit technology conference in Lisbon on Thursday in the hours after CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation.

Huang’s departure followed a series of allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an Nvidia employee and one with a woman who has been identified as a possible Chinese spy. The company, whose computer chips are at the core of generative AI’s disruptive powers, is valued at around $4 trillion, making it one of the most valuable in the world. A co-founder, Huang has been with Nvidia since its earliest days three decades ago, making it hard to imagine the company without him at the helm.

There’s nothing quite like a salacious, market-moving scandal to create a buzz at a tech event. The Web Summit organizers leaned into the news, quickly assembling a panel of tech experts to discuss whether Nvidia was bigger than its CEO.

Nothing in the allegations changes the fact that Huang is probably the godfather of the AI revolution, said investor and financial writer Adam Kobeissi. “He was the central figure,” Kobeissi said, even if he wasn’t the only person responsible for Nvidia’s success.

“This company is going to survive and thrive with or without him,” he added. “I don’t think this is some sort of bubble-popping moment where everything comes crumbling down.”

Sweeping financial investments and expectations across the AI industry have driven stock prices and company valuations to dizzying heights, with many critics warning of a bubble just waiting to burst with destabilizing effects. As powerful as Nvidia has become, it could be caught in the center of such a maelstrom.

While such a concentration of power is not the way to create resilient companies, said Ryan LaSalle, CEO of cybersecurity company Nisos, like Kobeissi he thinks Nvidia will weather the storm.

Interim Nvidia CEO Collette Kress, who has been with the company since 2013, is known for having a ton of loyalty within Nvidia, he said. “In a company of that much brainpower, there will be some natural leaders who can help shepherd them to the next chapter.”

One big question put to panel participants was whether Nvidia’s board made a mistake allowing one person to have so much power.

It wasn’t just a mistake of corporate culture, said Carissa Veliz, associate professor of philosophy at the Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI. It was also a mistake in terms of democracy.

For one person to wield so much power over decisions affecting the economy and national security means something has gone wrong and has revealed how vulnerable we are, Veliz said. If we look at the history of corporations, she said, there used to be a tradition of proving to the government that you were doing good for your country to earn your right to exist and get certain tax breaks.

“At the moment, we have shifted from that kind of framework to a framework in which a corporation is allowed to be essentially a kind of psychopath that only cares about its own profits, that only has duties to shareholders and which can be structured in any way, including a very powerful CEO with very little oversight,” she said.

Gil Duran, author of The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, said that he thought Nvidia’s errors in the lead-up to this moment would be studied in business and public relations crisis management classes.

“The board was completely missing out on most of the truth and the facts,” he said, referencing news reports that said Huang a year ago hired a law firm known for covering up sex scandals and President Donald Trump in May had been told about the CEO’s affair with the alleged Chinese spy.

“I don’t think there’s any other way to look at it but a catastrophe,” he said.

Duran and Veliz agreed that it was time to ensure tech CEOs face real oversight.

“These guys face no accountability and no supervision, and that’s part of the problem,” said Veliz. “These kind of small kings have their own small kingdoms… and they get away with almost anything.”

CEOs like Elon Musk at SpaceX and Sam Altman at OpenAI have enormous influence not only in their own companies but also across the national economy.

What we’re seeing in Huang’s downfall is the shattering of a myth about genius founders, said Duran. He questioned whether it would spark actual change, however, given that the market’s addiction to the narrative of great, powerful founders.

“The fact that they can just tumble markets with their personal lives that become geopolitical crises – this is an insane amount of power to outsource,” he said.

If we can tone down the myth, this moment provides a chance to look at where we’ve gone wrong and do better, Veliz said. There’s opportunity here, she added – to raise up companies that can build the kinds of technology we need, support democracies rather than erode them, aren’t based on surveillance and prediction, and can behave transparently.

For every other tech behemoth out there, there is plenty to be learned from Huang’s downfall. The concentration of power in one individual is not, as LaSalle pointed out, a safe long-term strategy.

What’s needed is more oversight and accountability from a company’s board of directors. In announcing Huang’s resignation, Nvidia also said it was appointing its first chairman for its board.

Huang’s entanglement with a potential honeypot is also an opportunity for tech companies to think about security, said LaSalle. No matter how sophisticated cybersecurity threats are becoming in the age of AI, he added, “people are still the simplest way in.”

Duran warned about the potential damage ahead if we fail to seize this as a moment to change. “If you look at the AI CEO vision of the future, it’s massive economic destruction so that a handful of people can become trillionaires,” he said. “No one voted for that. Nobody wants that, and we have a short window of time to collapse it before they collapse us.”

Disclosure: Katie Collins traveled to Lisbon as a guest of Web Summit to serve as a panel moderator. Her reporting from the event was independent of that role.

Siri isn’t smart enough for Apple’s next big things — and fans might not wait around

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

We posted two reviews of new Apple products this week in the Apple HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K, and there was one common theme. Apple’s Siri AI still isn’t good enough.

In fact, I’d argue that there’s still such a large gap between Siri and other AI assistants like Gemini, ChatGPT, Alexa+ and Muse that people could start to defect to other brands if Apple doesn’t get its act together. And soon.

For example, my colleague Mike Prospero compared the new HomeView against Amazon’s Echo Show 8 with Alexa+, and he found that Apple’s assistant isn’t nearly as capable. Mike could easily order a pizza through Uber Eats with Amazon’s device while Apple’s Siri just offered to make a call. Siri is not the AI agent you’ve been looking for.

Meanwhile, Engadget pointed out that Siri AI gets dumber the moment your iPhone is not within range. It defaults to generic world-knowledge answers. And Joanna Stern noted in her review that Siri stumbled on multi-step household tasks and at one point refused to open her front door despite recognizing her face.

It also didn’t help that the HomeView Siri started “talking” to other phone-based Siris in the house.

To be clear, Siri AI has improved versus previous versions, but it’s still quite limited as an everyday assistant compared to Google Gemini, Alexa+, ChatGPT, and Muse. And I’d argue that the longer Siri continues to lag, the more Apple is leaving the door open for competitors to overtake Apple.

Apple Intelligence, such as it is, also graces the new Apple TV 4K, a streaming device that costs a whopping $299. Apple is justifying the premium partly by touting the fact that Siri is inside, which is supposed to help you find things to watch.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

But things didn’t go very well in our testing. When Mike asked Siri to find scary movies for kids, Siri first responded “I’m not finding anything for that.” Then on the second attempt asking for scary movies good for kids the recommendations were nightmare fuel like “Poltergeist,” “Alien,” and “Seven.”

Meanwhile, the Google TV Streamer and Fire TV returned recommendations like “Coraline,” “Goosebumps 2,” “Hocus Pocus,” and “The Addams Family.”

Asking “What’s that movie with Audrey Hepburn that takes place in Rome” resulted in a bunch of Christmas movies, none with Hepburn. Though, Siri AI performed better with Tom Hanks action flicks.

Apple’s assistant has gotten better on the iPhone, especially with personal context. For example, I asked Siri AI to find the message from my daughter asking about earrings as a gift.

You can also perform multiple actions at once using your voice. I recently had it look up restaurants around Bryant Park that are rated 4 stars or higher but under $50 for lunch and then craft an outgoing message that includes the address for each and top dish. It worked seamlessly.

However, Siri AI is still missing two big things versus other assistants: live voice chat with video and powerful agentic features.

It’s not a good sign that I’ve now mapped Gemini Live to the Action button on my iPhone 17 Pro Max. That’s because I use Google’s voice assistant in combination with live video all of the time to ask questions and troubleshoot things around the house.

For example, I was able to fix a cantilever umbrella because Gemini could see what I was talking about and offer advice in real time. With Siri AI, you can share what’s on your screen but not a live video feed.

It’s getting to the point where I wish I could say “Hey, Gemini” to my iPhone.

Agentic AI is still in a nascent stage, but this is yet another area where Siri is still behind. In fact, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman recently reported that new CEO John Ternus has explicitly asked for the Siri AI team to speed things up here.

Right now you just can’t do things like book an Uber with Siri or perform complex tasks that Siri can work on in the background.

Assuming AI continues to be a driving force in consumer electronics, Apple could fall further behind in mind share and eventually lose market share.

Just this week I tried Google’s new Intelligent Eyewear glasses, which start at $395 and essentially put Gemini on your face. You can use these specs, made by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, to do everything from take calls and listen to music to get turn-by-turn directions and even real-time translation.

And because Gemini is truly live through the onboard camera, it can “see” what you see to answer questions or give advice on the fly. And, yes, they work with the iPhone.

Apple is reportedly working on its own Apple glasses, as well as an AI pendant and AirPods with cameras — all powered by Siri.

But I don’t think any of these new categories will take off for Apple unless Siri is up to snuff. Hey, Siri... the clock is ticking.

#3084. Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key – how it works

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Smart Home > Home Security

Google is moving digital keys out of individual smart lock apps and into the Google Wallet.

Google is adding digital home keys to Google Wallet, letting users tap their phones to unlock compatible smart locks. The home key functionality, which will integrate with Google Home, will roll out this month.

Also: This tiny box gives your older tech smart home superpowers

Apple introduced Home Keys in 2021 with iOS 15, allowing users to store digital keys in the Apple Wallet. This lets you tap your iPhone or Apple Watch on the lock to unlock it. More recently, the addition of Express Mode to Apple Home lets users unlock smart locks without first unlocking their iPhones with Face ID.

Google’s digital keys use tap-to-unlock via NFC on smart locks. Like the Apple Home Key, you don’t need to unlock your phone to use your digital key, though you can change your verification settings as you wish.

Google’s announcement confirms that the company is embracing Aliro and UWB unlocking technologies as well. UWB unlocking for smart locks is supported on Google Pixel 10 Pro and newer models, as well as select UWB-enabled Samsung Galaxy phones. Aliro is a common standard for compatible smart locks and devices.

Before Google’s announcement, compatible smart locks could be controlled on Android through their accompanying app and Google Home. Smart lock companies also offered their own digital access methods, like NFC cards, Bluetooth, and geolocation.

One digital key will be created for each Google Home, so it can unlock all compatible smart locks in that home. You won’t need to search through digital keys in Google Wallet to find the one for your front door, back door, or bedroom door — just tap your phone and Google Home will recognize the lock as one in your smart home ecosystem.

At launch, Google Wallet will support digital keys for the Aqara U400 with UWB and NFC, and NFC on the Schlage Sense Pro and Nuki Keypad 2.

Google Wallet already supports digital car keys for compatible vehicles.

#3083. What Is T-Mix? Navigating T-Mobile’s All-New Phone Plans and Perk Scheme

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

With a new system of "Picks," T-Mobile lets customers mix and match mobile add-ons.

T-Mobile is remixing its unlimited phone plans and introducing a structure where customers choose which services, like streaming video subscriptions or phone financing, apply to their accounts. Called T-Mix, the lineup is available now and includes four core plans that include “Picks” that can be mixed and matched every 90 days.

“T-Mobile and [other carriers] have really built a ‘good/better/best’ world” where customers choose prepackaged plans, Allan Samson, T-Mobile chief marketing officer, said during a call with CNET. “We’re going to blow that whole thing up, and you get to individually curate every experience you want.”

Much like with Verizon’s current plans, T-Mobile’s new offerings let customers pick and choose the perks they want rather than reserving some perks for certain plan tiers, as it had with its former Experience plan options. If you wanted a perk such as Hulu streaming, you had to pay up for the pricier Experience Beyond 2.0 plan. Conversely, even if you picked the Beyond plan for another reason, like unlimited mobile hotspot data, you still got Hulu whether you watched it or not.

Each of the new T-Mix plans includes a core set of high-speed data, hotspot data, video streaming speeds and international options. On top of that – and the feature that gives T-Mix its name – is a selection of Picks, which work like a type of currency to choose perks like streaming services, game passes, and services like DoorDash or T-Satellite. Picks can also go toward financing a new phone.

T-Mix replaces the existing Experience 2.0 plans for new customers, though existing customers can stay on their plans.

Despite the modular nature of Picks, T-Mobile is still sticking with its one-plan-fits-all policy for accounts with multiple lines. Unlike Verizon and AT&T, where each family member can have their own plan, everyone needs to agree on which T-Mix base to start from: Standard, More, Loaded and T-Mix Saver. The number of Picks you get depends on the plan and the number of lines on the account.

The Standard plan includes 50GB of high-speed 5G data, unlimited hotspot data at 3G speeds, unlimited international data while traveling in Canada and Mexico at 2G speeds, unlimited texting in more than 215 countries and up to 480p (SD) streaming resolution. A single line includes one Pick.

The More plan includes unlimited high-speed data, up to 60GB of high-speed hotspot data (which drops down to an unlimited amount at 3G speeds), 15GB of high-speed data in Canada and Mexico (then unlimited at 256Kbps), up to 5GB of high-speed data when traveling internationally (then unlimited at 256Kbps) and up to 4K (UHD) streaming resolution. A single line on More includes two picks.

The Loaded plan also includes unlimited high-speed data, up to 250GB of hotspot data (then unlimited at 3G speeds), 30GB of high-speed data in Canada and Mexico (then unlimited at 256Kbps), up to 15GB high-speed data when traveling (and down to 256Kbps unlimited after reaching that cap) and up to 4K (UHD) streaming resolution. On the Loaded plan, you can also connect a cellular-enabled device, such as a smartwatch or tablet, for $5 an item. A single line includes three Picks.

For those who want just basic phone service, the T-Mix Saver plan includes the same features as the Standard plan, but does not include Picks and is limited to two lines.

All plans include unlimited texting when traveling in more than 215 countries, long-distance calling at $0.50 a minute and T-Mobile’s Basic Scam Shield service.

For each plan, you can choose to finance a new phone using T-Mobile’s Standard 36-month term or the recently introduced Flex 36-month commitment that rolls in all of the upfront costs.

Pricing (with AutoPay and not including taxes and fees) for the Standard plan starts at $55 for a single line, jumps to $85 for two lines (or $42.50 a line) and then increases to $100 for three lines (or $33.33 a line). Additional lines cost $15 more apiece.

The More plan starts at $75 for one line, then goes to $130 for two lines and $155 for three lines. Additional lines add $25 each to the monthly cost.

The Loaded plan is $95 for a single line, $160 for two lines and $200 for three lines. Adding more Loaded lines costs $40 each.

The Saver plan costs $45 for a single line and $80 for two lines (the maximum number allowed). T-Mobile is currently running a promotion that brings those prices down to $30 and $65 if you switch from another provider and bring along your phone number.

An account on the first three plans can have up to 12 lines.

One advantage of T-Mobile’s now-old Experience plans was the simplicity of knowing that if you moved up to a higher tier such as Experience Beyond, you’d get a specific set of additional perks.

Picks gives you the flexibility to only activate perks you’ll actually use, but working out which to opt for is a bit complex. With Picks, there are two components at play: How many Picks you get on your account, and when you can change them. It sounds low-key chaotic on the surface, but it will start to make more sense, I promise.

T-Mobile assigns a Pick value to the perks it’s offering. For example, one Pick could get you Netflix Standard with ads or the DashPass service by DoorDash. If you want an Apple Music Individual or Google AI Pro subscription, that would use two Picks.

Higher-tier offerings such as Netflix Standard and Xbox Game Pass Ultimate are three Picks each, while Netflix Premium and ESPN Unlimited are four Picks.

Those are all services offered by T-Mobile partners, and can change over time (more on this in a moment).

T-Mobile also has its own Picks services. T-Satellite can be activated with one Pick, and so can the company’s new Optimized Video Calling service, which gives video calls a higher data priority for better quality.

If you’re looking to buy a new phone, you could get one for between one and three Picks depending on the device — in other words, you can forgo fancy add-on perks to get discounts on a new handset. Phone picks automatically inherit the Flex 36-month financing term.

To give Picks a real-world analogy, picture a restaurant buffet. You’re given a plate that’s sized based on how many Picks are available to your account. A Standard plan with one line would have the smallest plate (one Pick), while a Loaded plan with four lines would have a much larger plate (11 Picks).

The Picks on an account can be pooled depending on the group’s needs. A family of four on the Loaded plan, for example, might decide to get Netflix Premium to watch movies without ads (4 Picks), DashPass to save money on food deliveries (1 Pick), Xbox Game Pass Premium (2 Picks) and Pandora Plus (1 Pick) for entertainment and then a new phone for Mom (3 Picks).

The number of Picks you get depends on the plan and how many lines it includes. Not using a Pick doesn’t lower the plan price, and you’re not able to pay more for extra Picks (like adding a Verizon perk, for example) aside from moving to a more expensive plan.

Also, Picks are separate from the company’s perks such as T-Mobile Tuesdays promotions, discounts on hotels and rental cars, Delta premium in-flight drinks and MLB TV.

The next Picks component is timing. Every 90 calendar days, you can switch your Picks. Did you burn through all the shows you wanted to watch on Hulu? At the next Picks window, you can switch it for another option, or dump some 1- and 2-value Picks and pool them to get a new phone.

If you’re in the middle of the schedule and want to pick up Netflix to see what everyone is talking about in season four of The Diplomat, you can do that by canceling an existing Pick service and adding the streaming service for a fee, which Samson said would be in the $10 to $15 range. Or, at any time you can move up to a plan with more Picks (such as from More to Loaded).

The exceptions to that timing are T-Mobile’s Picks; you could turn on T-Satellite if you know you’re going remote backpacking, as long as a Pick is available in your plan.

#3082. Micron Technology vs. Qualcomm: Which Tech Stock Is the Better Buy for 2027?

One of these chipmakers is riding a record AI-driven surge, while the other is working to reinvent itself beyond the smartphone.

Semiconductors power everything from smartphones to massive artificial intelligence (AI) servers. Choosing between high-growth memory leaders and diversified wireless giants like Micron Technology (MU -2.52%) and QUALCOMM (QCOM -2.64%) is a pivotal decision for investors today.

Micron Technology focuses on the memory and storage components essential for modern computing. Qualcomm provides the processors and modems that connect the world. Comparing these semiconductor leaders helps clarify where the next wave of growth might originate as we look toward 2027.

Micron Technology specializes in memory and storage solutions, primarily manufacturing DRAM and NAND chips for smartphones and artificial intelligence servers. The company now generates approximately 60% of its revenue from the data center market. Because its top ten customers account for over half of its total revenue, customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 3, 2026, revenue reached nearly $133 billion. This represents a significant revenue growth of approximately 256% compared to the prior year. The company reported a net income of roughly $85 billion during this period, driven by high demand for high-bandwidth memory products.

As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 0x. This ratio measures total debt, including both short- and long-term obligations, against shareholders' equity, and a value of zero suggests the company has negligible debt. The current ratio of 3.3x indicates ample assets to cover short-term liabilities, and it generated nearly $59.0 billion in free cash flow in the fiscal year ended Sept. 3, 2026.

Qualcomm designs the modems and processors that power millions of mobile devices while diversifying into the automotive and Internet of Things markets. Apple and Samsung are major customers, with each representing 10% or more of total revenues. This reliance on large partners means Qualcomm remains a central player in the semiconductor industry.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 27, 2026, revenue reached nearly $43 billion. This was a slight decline, as revenue growth was approximately- 2.6% over the previous year. Despite the dip in sales, the company achieved a net income of roughly $13.6 billion, aided by its high-margin patent licensing business.

As of its September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.5x, reflecting a moderate use of total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio of 1.9x indicates it can comfortably cover short-term liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Sept. 27, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $8.7 billion.

Micron Technology faces significant volatility in chip prices, leading to unpredictable revenue cycles. It deals with intense competition in the data center market and regulatory challenges stemming from restrictions imposed on its products by the Chinese government. The company must also manage the costs of massive expansion projects while competing against rivals like Samsung and SK Hynix.

Qualcomm faces high revenue concentration from mobile handset makers, who are increasingly seeking to develop their own internal modems. This shift toward vertical integration, especially by customers like Apple, could reduce future demand for its connectivity products. The company also faces substantial exposure to trade tensions in China and ongoing legal challenges regarding its patent licensing practices.

Investors must choose between the lower Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates and the lower P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

The company is expanding into the data center market, targeting $5 billion in revenue by fiscal 2027 and $15 billion in data center revenue by fiscal 2029. It is also seeing rapid growth in its automotive segment.

Moreover, Qualcomm is not dependent on growing investment in new data centers. It is aiming to gain share of existing spending. This makes it a potentially safer stock to ride the data center boom, especially given the prospect of additional guardrails on new data center construction following the midterm elections.

Micron is too sensitive to memory pricing for me to be comfortable holding the stock beyond 2027. It might continue to hit new highs over the next 12 months, but in the longer term, I think Qualcomm has a more durable business that can still deliver market-beating returns to shareholders in 2027 and through the end of the decade.

The best Garmin watches are always a feature of the Black Friday sales, and if you’ve been patiently waiting for the brand’s line-up to get discounted, that patience has been rewarded.

With a new option called Memory summary, you’re able to view the details that Gemini has gathered about you over time. These may be tidbits from your conversations or things that you directly told the AI. Even better, you can add or remove any details just by editing the memory or issuing your request directly to Gemini.

This new capability is available in Gemini across the board, so you can access it at the Gemini website, in the mobile iOS and Android apps, and in the Windows and Mac desktop apps.

Launch Gemini via the web or in one of the mobile or desktop apps. In the left pane displaying your previous chats, select the Settings icon at the bottom. At the Settings screen, select Personal Intelligence and then click or tap Memory summary. If the option is grayed out, it means the Memory feature is turned off. To proceed, turn it back on. You can always turn if off again afterward if you wish.

You’ll then see the individual details by category. My summary arranged the information across such categories as Essentials, Business & Career, Reading & Interests, and Culinary Preferences. Go down the list to see the individual items in each category. To view a recent history, tap the three dot-icon at the top and select Memory history. This shows you the latest changes and updates to Gemini’s memory.

Also: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents

What if Gemini’s memory includes details that are too personal or just incorrect? No problem. You can alter the AI’s memories of you. At the website or in one of the desktop apps, click the pencil icon at the top. Now you’re able to directly edit the text to add, remove, or revise specific details. After you’ve made your changes, just click Save.

For example, my summary said that that I lived in Madison County. I have no idea where Gemini got that notion as I live in New York. Here, I revised the text and saved the changes, which then synced across the Gemini website and apps.

The mobile apps have no direct editing capability. But there’s another method that works both on mobile and on the desktop. Just tell Gemini what change you want to make. At the prompt, type and speak your request, and the AI will carry it out for you.

As an example, my summary said that I run a business called Batter Up selling collectible baseball cards. That’s not at all true. I had once referred to such a store only to test Gemini’s image creation skills to design a logo for a baseball card seller. Here, I simply told Gemini that I don’t run a business called Batter Up and asked it to remove that item from its memory. Poof, that detail quickly disappeared.

#3079. Animaj Brings ‘Ozzy Fox’ Series to Disney Plus as It Charts a Path for AI in Animation

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Animators using agentic AI? It's already happening, and this is what it looks like.

A lot has changed since I first met the team behind Animaj at Walt Disney Studios in Burbank, California, in 2025. Since teasing an upcoming project with Disney a year ago, the AI-boosted animation studio has now produced Ozzy Fox, its first combined project with the animation powerhouse.

Debuting on YouTube and Disney Junior in July and launching on streaming service Disney Plus soon, the preschool-age show features bright colors, catchy songs and a cute family of foxes. It’s drawn and animated by humans, but with an AI assist to speed things up.

In the last year, AI has become a more normalized part of the creative process, popping up everywhere from music to movies. Studios don’t shy away from saying “AI” anymore; they’re using it to make content faster while — at least in some cases — still keeping humans in jobs.

Animaj recently released FlipMove, a “pipeline” combining all of the AI models it has been developing over the past few years into a single tool for its animators to use. The studio has also created an agentic AI workflow, Animaj CEO and co-founder Sixte de Vauplane told the media during the 2026 Disney Accelerator Demo Day.

So what does agentic AI mean for animation? A bunch of agents that have access to AI tools and context about the show so they know when to use each tool, de Vauplane told me last week in Burbank.

“We had one agent reading the notes, another one coordinating to see which kind of model we have to use,” he told me. “Here, what we wanted is to build the ultimate pipeline, CGI pipeline, for animators, for directors, that is built on a closed ecosystem of data.”

The point of AI is to reduce the time from the director’s initial notes on a storyline to the final cut being produced, he said.

“If you can do twice the notes in the same amount of time, that means twice better in terms of quality, and that’s overall what the industry is looking for,” de Vauplane said. “This use of AI, which is artistic-centric, is really the answer we think the industry should embrace.”

Animaj animators have “full control at every frame,” de Vauplane told us. Its closed, in-house LLMs have access to context about the show, drawing style, characters and storylines so that suggestions are customized and fit in with what the team wants to achieve.

When I first met the team in 2025, they told me their technology doesn’t replace animators; it simply making their jobs less tedious. An animator sketches out each of the main poses of the characters, and then AI is used to fill in all the in-between movements of the character that could stem from each pose. An animator tweaks those poses before they’re finalized.

A demo video of the new FlipMove pipeline shows a human-drawn sketch being quickly transformed into a 3D animation, with the AI tools importing the Ozzy Fox house and characters onto the screen, and then also posing them to match the sketch.

The writers and animators involved still have their jobs, David Min, vice president of Disney Innovation, told me; they’re just making content a lot more quickly.

Animaj also recently published its AI manifesto online, calling slop, not AI, the enemy. AI slop is low-quality content being rapidly generated by simple prompts using AI tools online. According to Animaj, collaborative AI tools should be put in the hands of storytellers, “because rejecting AI leaves more ground to those producing slop.”

Read more: The New Adobe Firefly AI Is All About Video Editing

Its anti-slop message followed headlines upon the release of Ozzy Fox in July that accused it of being AI slop, citing hallmarks such as unfinished backgrounds and the lack of letters and numbers on objects in the show.

The show wasn’t AI-generated; it was created and drawn by humans, with details filled in by AI tools and checked by more humans. But it raises the question: Is slop in the eye of the beholder? And how much AI is enough to call it slop?

The manifesto also argues that AI reduces the cost and speeds up the production of human-created animation, but that every hour saved should be poured back into that human work.

“AI makes more ideas affordable to try: the strange character, the unfamiliar culture, the story nobody would have greenlit,” Animaj says. “We can put them in front of families, learn what moves them and go again.”

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

Is Android Settings not delivering enough power? The Essentials app features 30+ mods and tweaks - but you won't find it in the Play Store

Most Android owners know of the Settings app, which gives them all the power Google assumes they need. Then there’s the Developer Options feature that can be enabled to give users even more power.

Also: I turned an old Android phone into a server for my LAN

If that’s not enough, there’s now Essentials, a power-user’s toolbox that includes 30+ mods and tweaks for things like button remapping, app freezing, Google Maps battery saving modes, sound and haptics, wallpaper, widgets, status bar icon customization, edge lighting, flashlight pulsing, notification management, Always-On Display, and more.

The only requirement for most Essentials features is Android 8 or newer. There are a handful of advanced features that require shell providers like Shizuku or even root access, but the majority of features most users will want to enable have no requirements beyond the minimum.

Essentials isn’t found on the Google Play Store. Instead, Essentials must be sideloaded from the APK available on its official GitHub Repository. Keep in mind that Google has changed the way apps are sideloaded.

Also: How to sideload Android apps on your phone now

Make sure you understand the new sideloading process before you proceed. You’ll also need to change some permissions, depending on the feature you want to use. For example, to change lock screen shortcuts, you have to enable it in Accessibility Services.

As well, you have to enable restricted settings, which is done with Settings > Apps > See all X apps > Essentials. On that page, tap the three-dot menu and then tap “Allow restricted settings.”

Without that feature enabled, Essentials will be hamstrung by Android’s permissions system.

Essentials is fairly simple to use. You open the app, search for the feature you want to enable, and enable it. One thing you’ll discover is that you have to enable a lot of permissions for Essentials. It seems every time I go to enable or customize a feature, I have to grant yet another permission. I know it sounds like a hassle, but given the extra power you gain, it’s worth it.

Also: How to turn on Android’s Private DNS mode

Let me walk you through a feature found in Essentials you’ll wish were baked into Android. The feature is App Lock, which lets you require authentication for specific apps. This is a handy option, especially if someone gets ahold of your phone while it’s unlocked and tries to open certain apps you’d prefer to keep private (such as your banking app). To use this feature, you have to grant Essentials permission for Accessibility features, which you’ll be prompted to do when you go to enable it.

On the next page, tap “Select locked apps,” and you’ll be prompted to select the apps that require authentication to open. For instance, I want to make sure that Authy (my 2FA app of choice), my bank app, and Messages require authentication before they open. To do that, I tap the On/Off slider for those apps until they are in the On position. The next time I go to open any of those apps, I’ll be required to authenticate via the fingerprint sensor.

Also: This silent Android feature scans your photos for ‘sensitive content’

Another handy feature is found in Notifications and Alerts, where you can enable notification lighting, flashlight pulse, notification snoozing, and snooze system notifications. You can enable notification lighting and then select which apps it applies to. I enabled notification lighting for Messages and Phone, so I will never miss a message or call, even if my phone is on silent mode. You can also enable flashlight pulses, so it doesn’t matter if your phone’s screen is facing up or down — you’ll be notified of your messages.

That’s essentially how Essentials works. Do remember two things: you’ll be met with a barrage of permission requests, and some of those permissions aren’t possible unless you have root access or Shizuku (an open-source Android tool that lets third-party apps use system-level APIs and ADB (Android Debug Bridge) privileges without requiring you to fully root your device. Also, note that Shizuku requires you to enable wireless debugging to start the service. Once you install Shizuku (from the Play Store), you’ll find detailed (and lengthy) directions on how to do this.

Also: 5 ways I speed up your Android phone beyond clearing system cache

If you want considerably more control over your Android device, I highly recommend adding Essentials, as you won’t find most of these options in any other tool.

#3076. Why Chefs Save Leftover Pasta Water, and Why You Should, Too

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

If you're skipping this step when making pasta, you're leaving behind liquid gold.

Among the suggestions home cooks often hear about unforgivable pasta sins, two top the list: overcooking and underseasoning. But you’ve already got this! You know to ignore the recommended cooking time by a minute or two, understanding that crossover cooking and/or added sauce will keep moving the needle toward perfect al dente, and you’re absolutely in the habit of salting your pasta cooking water to a degree that’s “like the sea.”

Those two steps are crucial to get the best outcome for your pasta, no matter the shape, and they deserve top billing. But the world’s most practiced pasta cooks also follow a third maxim: Save your pasta water.

I spoke to three chefs about why hanging onto this liquid gold is a habit you should always practice, no matter what kind of sauce you have — or even if there’s no sauce — simmering nearby.

When pasta meets boiling water, it absorbs the seasoned liquid and releases starch. After its cooking time of roughly 5 to 10 minutes (shape and size dependent), what’s left over is almost akin to a stock and should be treated accordingly. While 10-minute pasta water may not have the texture and flavor of a long-simmered stock, it still delivers broth. Why toss it?

“Pasta water is starchy, and when added to a sauce, it helps to bind the sauce to the pasta when the pasta and sauce are tossed together,” said chef Melissa Mastrianni-Oleary, founder of Keeping It Simple Italian. “It also helps prevent the sauce from drying out during tossing.”

“If you ever hear your pasta sizzling in the pan as it cooks with your sauce, it’s your cue to add more pasta water to the pan,” said Jessica Mode, culinary instructor of Homebody Eats. “This sound means all of your liquid has cooked off, and you’ll need the water to keep the pasta hydrated and the sauce creamy.”

When creaminess is the goal, the starchiness of the pasta water also acts as a natural thickener or emulsifier when it meets one or more other ingredients likely in your sauce.

“The pasta water especially helps when doing buttery sauces,” said Ciro Fodera, culinary director of Capri Italian Steakhouse. “The starchy water allows the butter to emulsify into the sauce, giving that rich and creamy gloss of a properly made cacio e pepe.”

While we’re on the subject of cacio, a ladle of pasta water also keeps shredded cheese from clumping in your pan. The starchy water also helps emulsify non-dairy ingredients, such as olive oil, into something that looks and feels creamy.

Taking your pasta pot to the sink and draining all that goodness away is both unforgivable and unnecessary.

If that seems risky, messy, or time-consuming — admittedly, it takes practice — use a glass measuring cup to scoop out a generous amount of cooking liquid right before draining or set a pot or bowl in your sink to catch the drained water.

Pasta pots with built-in colanders are also made for this. The more pasta water you save, the more you have to work with, both for the dish in progress and for the future. More on that below.

Combining your cooked pasta with your sauce and adding a bit of pasta water to marry it all relies on intuition, but you can set yourself up for success with some practiced guidance.

Start by undercooking your pasta. Yes, perhaps even more so than you already are. “You only want to slightly cook the pasta in boiling water,” said Mode.

“After that, you’ll transfer the pasta to the pan with your sauce in it. During this process, you’ll ladle the pasta water along the side of the pan,” she said, while cautioning not to dump it directly on top of the pasta so that it emulsifies the sauce rather than gets further absorbed by the noodles.

“Next, turn your heat to high and vigorously stir the pasta around,” Mode said. “The high heat, plus movement, in combination with pasta water is what gives you restaurant-quality pasta that’s perfectly cooked, with a creamy, jammy emulsion.”

“I like to toss the pasta for a good 2 to 3 minutes so the pasta picks up the sauce and pasta water,” said Mastrianni-Oleary. “Sauce should not sit on top of pasta. The sauce should be absorbed by the pasta and flavor it a little from the inside.”

Since it’s contributing flavor, Mastrianni-Oleary also notes another important consideration: “Not all pasta water is created equal,” she said. “Really good pasta water starts with really good pasta. Cheaper pasta does not produce great pasta water, so I prefer slightly more expensive pastas like Rummo.”

Also, because you’ve generously seasoned your pasta water, keep that in mind when you first season your sauce. “I definitely have underestimated how salty my sauces can be when adding pasta water,” said Fodera.

“Generally, the rule is to make sure you start your sauce with only a little salt. When you add the pasta water, it should increase the amount of salt to the perfect amount,” he said. “You can always add [salt], but you can’t take it away.”

Saving pasta water for sauce cooking alongside the pasta is arguably mandatory, but as a present to future you, consider setting some aside for other projects where pasta isn’t actively cooking.

“You can definitely freeze the pasta water,” said Fodera. Let it cool, then portion it into small containers or even an ice cube tray.

“I’d use it for soups,” said Mastrianni-Oleary. “It will add a little starchiness to the soup along with salt.” A natural thickener and seasoning agent, reserved pasta water can also be used when cooking other grains.

Plus, freezing your pasta water is a failsafe. “I’ve definitely been at home and not paying attention, so I dump all of my pasta water out in the sink,” Fodera said. “I’ll just pop an ice cube of the pasta water to finish my sauce with, so I don’t lose any of that flavor.”

#3073. After 3 Weeks and More Than 451,000 Folds, the iPhone Duo’s Hinge Is Finally Starting to Fail

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

We built a machine to fold the iPhone Duo until it breaks. Twenty days of 24/7 folding later, Apple's phone shows the first major sign of wear.

Three weeks ago, we put Apple’s new iPhone Duo on our custom foldable phone testing rig, the Fold-a-Phone, to find out how many times it could fold until it broke. It’s not fully broken yet, but the hinge has started to break down.

I initially detected some looseness in the hinge motion yesterday during our afternoon livestream. It became evident that the iPhone Duo was not opening with the same firm sound I was used to hearing. When I left the office last night at 6 p.m., it was still opening completely flat.

Now, however, the screen no longer opens all the way flat. Instead, it unfolds most of the way but leaves a few degrees of angle in the hinge. Check out the video above to see for yourself.

After examining the sensor data we’ve collected, and the photos and videos we shoot constantly during the testing process, we determined that changes in the opening force and motion began occurring around the 390,000-fold point on Tuesday afternoon and gradually built until last night.

The wire we use to open the phone screen would withdraw before the screen was in the fully open position, but it would then sort of “coast” the rest of the way down. But between 12:30 and 1 a.m. this morning, around 440,300 folds, the screen would no longer have time to open all the way before the Fold-a-Phone caused it to close again.

How serious is this issue? In the grand scheme of things, not very. The phone still operates and maintains other screen positions without issue. There’s no cracking, signs of a more visible crease or other failures.

This issue is not sufficient to meet our established failure conditions in the Duo, which include loss of power, sensors failing to detect the screen where it needs to be within the given timeframe, and screen blackout. The phone is only about 5 to 10 degrees away from the fully open state, and it can still be moved the rest of the way by hand (though without the distinctive snap sound and feel it had earlier).

Join CNET’s iPhone Duo livestream on YouTube weekdays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. ET, where you can follow along live and watch the Fold-a-Phone do its thing to a Duo.

Chances are, if you had bought the phone and encountered this behavior, you might not even notice it at first. And, remember, by the time this started, we’d subjected the iPhone Duo to the equivalent of nearly 12 and a half years of folding (assuming 100 folds per day) – well beyond the number of folds we’d expect from even an avid user.

Apple has not publicly stated the anticipated number of folds the iPhone Duo would endure, so we’ve been left to speculate. Guesses within CNET have ranged from 500,000 (matching Samsung’s rating for the Galaxy Z Fold 8) to 1.5 million. But even if we don’t yet know for sure how much worse the hinge action will become, and thus what the final number will be, what we’ve seen today represents the first significant step toward failure.

We are going to keep going. And we hope you’ll stick with us, both here and on our daily livestreams, to see what more unfolds.

#3070. Microsoft doesn’t ‘have an ETA for full recovery’ on outage yet

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

One think tank's estimate puts the cost of the outage at $7 billion.

Microsoft is making progress in resolving the massive global outage that started Thursday morning and affected Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Outlook access in 74 countries, according to Downdetector. But on Friday afternoon, the company said it wasn’t sure when the issue would be fully fixed.

“As infrastructure stabilizes, we’re still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic, so customers may see improved sign-in/access while delivery and processing continue to catch up,” Microsoft posted in its now long-running X thread about the outage. “We do not have an ETA for full recovery yet. Service access can recover before mail flow fully normalizes.”

For some frustrated X users in the comments, that might not be enough. While many users are back in Outlook and Teams, the outage has now been affecting some for over 24 hours. One think tank told CNN it estimated the outage resulted in $7 billion in losses, due to many businesses and organizations being unable to access their everyday systems.

Hope lesson has been learnt during the last 24 hours. Please deeply reflect on what went wrong and try not getting yourselves into these stressful situations again. Better for you, better for us as well.

On Friday morning, Microsoft shared an update on X that it was “seeing encouraging recovery progress” and that “a growing portion” of Microsoft 365 services was improving, noting in a follow-up post that it was seeing “broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.”

Also: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited

Downdetector reports have stayed low as of Friday midday at around 3,000.

“Some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue,” Microsoft said. “We’re focused on recovery for the remaining affected environments while prioritizing email queue and backlog reduction. The extended 48-hour email timeout window remains in place to help protect delayed messages as delivery catches up.”

Microsoft has not publicly identified the cause of the outage, but is maintaining it’s not security-related.

Also: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited

Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, said on X late Thursday night, “I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.”

Microsoft reiterated that late Friday morning in an update to its X thread on the outage.

“We will continue to share more information as we have it, and for now we can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity. Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward,” Microsoft wrote.

According to CNN, Microsoft told Australia’s Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke that they “don’t believe they are dealing with a cyber attack.” During a press conference, Burke said Microsoft told him “they believe they are dealing in some ways similar to what we saw with respect to CrowdStrike where there is an update that has gone awry.”

That refers to the great CrowdStrike meltdown of July 2024, in which a software issue disrupted operations at hospitals, airlines, and other major information hubs.

On Thursday morning, multiple people began reporting issues with Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, according to Downdetector. By 1 p.m. ET, the number of reported Outlook outages was nearly 83,000 but had fallen to just under 75,000 by 2:38 p.m. ET. Teams and Copilot reports started dropping significantly by Thursday evening, but many individuals were still reporting issues accessing systems well into Friday morning on X and Reddit. Even Microsoft’s status page was down until around 3 p.m. ET Thursday.

Also: If the November Windows update fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do

It’s unclear how many people the outage affected, though Microsoft’s own numbers from January say Microsoft 365 “exceeds 450 million commercial paid seats,” illustrating the scale of the issue.

After “restarting affected servers” Thursday afternoon, Microsoft added said at 2:31 p.m. ET.

“We determined the elevated load isn’t driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure,” the post said.

#3068. Can the Anthropic IPO Save the AI Rally?

AI stocks have had a rough month. Anthropic's debut offers some hope.

AI stocks fell for the second day in a row on Friday as investors continue to assess the fallout from Jensen Huang's sudden resignation as CEO of Nvidia.

More than any other business leader, Huang was at the center of the AI boom, a ubiquitous advocate for the revolutionary technology and a visionary strategist, whose company dominates the market for AI chips with roughly 90% market share of data center GPUs.

Huang's absence leaves a question mark hanging above not only Nvidia but also the broader AI sector, as Nvidia has become a financial backstop for an array of companies including neoclouds like CoreWeave and research labs like OpenAI. Those relationships and its so-called "circular financing" are expected to face more scrutiny with Huang out of the CEO chair, and Nvidia could scale back its widespread ambitions as it looks to reduce its financial exposure.

Investors looking for another catalyst to shift the narrative away from Huang's absence won't have to wait long. Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday, which would normally dominate the market calendar for the week, but the bigger news, and potential driver for AI stocks, is Anthropic's (Nasdaq: ANT) IPO.

Anthropic is set to start trading on Thursday, Nov. 19, and it will become the first AI lab to go public, beating rival OpenAI to market.

Anthropic has scaled back its offering, in part a response to increasing investor skepticism about the AI trade, and it's now targeting a valuation of $1.4 trillion, down from an expected $2 trillion earlier in the year.

At that valuation, the stock looks well-priced, especially compared to Space Exploration Technologies, the other blockbuster IPO this year, which soared after its June debut before retracing those gains.

The Claude parent reported run rate revenue of $81 billion for October, meaning it would trade at approximately 17 times sales, which puts it on par with software stocks like Snowflake and Datadog. However, Anthropic is reporting triple-digit revenue growth, an adjusting operating profit, and has established itself as the leading AI lab, which makes it significantly more attractive than the average SaaS stock.

That's a good sign that Anthropic stock will soar when it starts trading, as demand clearly outstrips the limited float of the stock. The company will employ a staggered lockup that will allow directors, officers, and non-founder employees to sell up to 10% of their holdings once the stock starts trading. Others will have to wait 180 days or longer for the initial lockup period to expire.

A surge in Anthropic stock on opening day is likely to cast a halo effect on the broader AI trade, as it will demonstrate both confidence in Anthropic, the leading AI lab, and therefore confidence in the long-term success of AI more broadly, as Anthropic is the best test case yet for AI.

Anthropic could displace Nvidia as the central stock in the AI narrative, as the success of labs like Anthropic and OpenAI will ultimately determine whether AI will be as transformative as investors hope. After all, Anthropic represents the AI product for sale: Claude and its derivatives, like Claude Code. Nvidia is just the "picks-and-shovels" play here. Nvidia dominates the market for those tools, but they're only valuable because investors expect generative AI and other AI iterations to unlock trillions of dollars of value.

When Anthropic goes public, it becomes the most direct vessel for that bet, and if the stock rises, it's likely to pull chip stocks and other AI players higher along with it. We’ll learn more on Thursday.

#3067. ‘We need more reviewers’: Finding Linux bugs is easy now – fixing them is another story

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Some Linux maintainers are quitting under the crushing strain of AI bug reports, while others see signs for hope.

Recently, Microsoft’s FORGE Lab reported that its AI scanning system, MDASH, turned up 59 upstream Linux kernel bug reports, including one flaw at least 21 years old. That’s less impressive than it sounds. For 2026, through Nov. 2, the Linux Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) team reported an average of 27 CVEs a day.

Why so many? Easy: in Linux, any bug can be a security bug. As Linux Torvalds told me in 2024, “Bugs will happen, and anything can be a security bug if somebody is clever enough to just figure out how to abuse it.” Besides, since Linux runs everything from smartphones to refrigerators to supercomputers, what may be a serious bug in one device may not even appear at all on another.

It’s not just Linux, though. In the latest Windows Patch Tuesday security release, Microsoft reported 726 CVEs. The vast majority of these bug reports are coming from AI programmers. Finding bugs on anything is no longer the hard part. But reviewing and fixing them is, and both Microsoft developers and kernel maintainers are struggling to keep up.

Also: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited

As the FORGE Lab said, “Finding bugs and fixing them are drastically out of balance.” Turning its findings into reports took more than four person-months because “human effort [is] the bottleneck.”

That’s hurting the overworked maintainers. On Nov. 10, an ARM engineer and Linux kernel maintainer Lorenzo Stoakes gave up reviewing code. He’d been a reviewer for the memory-management core, misc, reclaim, and Rust-related sections. Stoakes, a kernel contributor since 2014,  wrote, “Given the current throughput in the kernel resulting from AI-generated series, I unfortunately lack the bandwidth to generally be able to offer review except in those areas I maintain.”

Stoakes added, “Of course the AI wave has been horrible, and is getting significantly worse. At first it was once in a while that I’d see slop. Then it was at least once a week. Then every few days. Nowadays it’s pretty much half of what I see, if not more.”

Also: Filing bugs for open-source apps is a huge help for devs – and easier than you think

He’s not alone. As Greg Kroah-Hartman, the Linux kernel stable maintainer, said in a Q&A session at Open Source Summit Europe, “We don’t have enough people to review them, the onslaught of the LLM-generated patches. We need more reviewers. We don’t have enough. All of the maintainers are burnt out, and we have been for ten years.”

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. Linux Torvalds, Linux’s creator, said in a recent Linux Kernel Mailing List (LKML) message that much of the new code in the Linux 7.4 rc 2 “was driven by various AI fixes.”

He continued, “that on the bpf [Berkeley Packet Filter]- side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true. I think most other areas haven’t reached that point yet, but it’s at least a sign that we _may_ be starting to see the tide starting to turn. Don’t hold your breath, but maybe cross your fingers we’ll be getting there in the not entirely distant future.”

We can but hope. In an interview, Kroah-Hartman isn’t so optimistic. “We are getting closer, yes, but not quite there yet.”  He’s not even willing to give a guesstimate of when human-approved AI fixes will catch up with and overcome AI bug reports.

Also: I locked down my OpenClaw agent with Claude Code – then dared it to escape

Daniel Steinberg, the creator of the open-source cURL project, is also cautiously optimistic. Steinberg, who’s been especially critical of AI slop bug reports, told me in an interview that he now believes “we manage the flood pretty well so far, even if it goes a little up and down in periods depending exactly on who sends us a new set of findings this particular week.”

Still, while AI bugs remain a major headache for now, AI bug fixes, along with the work of thousands of maintainers, may finally be starting to stem the AI bug flood. I still foresee long days and nights of work ahead.

I also expect we’ll see more serious security breaches. In November alone, we saw a serious Linux TCP networking security hole revealed; the nasty Alpine Linux OpenSSH flaw; Alpine’s GitLab near-miss; and the wide-open PHP2Shell security problem, which many groups still haven’t patched.

#3066. SpaceX Attempts History Friday With the First-Ever Double Catch

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

SpaceX is going to catch the Super Heavy rocket and the upper stage of the Starship booster, something never done before.

A little over two years ago, SpaceX launched a Starship into orbit and then caught the Super Heavy booster when it returned to Earth, a feat it has since repeated multiple times. The company is taking the next step in rocket reusability by catching both the booster and the upper stage of its Starship on Flight 15, something never achieved before.

SpaceX is launching Flight 15 into orbit on Friday, Nov. 13, with the 75-minute launch window opening at 5:45 p.m. ET.

On its mission, the Starship will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites, orbit Earth 14 times and return on Saturday. All of that is in line with most of SpaceX’s launches, of which there have been over 280 dating back to 2025.

What makes the launch interesting is that SpaceX is attempting two things it hasn’t attempted before.

The first is catching its latest booster, the Super Heavy V3, using Mechazilla, the informal name SpaceX gave to the launch-and-catch tower located at its facility in Boca Chica, Texas. SpaceX has caught the Super Heavy V1 successfully three times, but this is the first for the V3 rocket. The tower will use its arms like chopsticks to catch the Super Heavy V3 out of midair.

The second is recovering both stages of the rocket. Prior Starship launches featured just the Super Heavy booster getting caught by Mechazilla while the upper stage landed in the ocean. This time around, SpaceX wants to catch the upper stage when it returns on Saturday with Mechazilla.

“The upcoming flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch,” SpaceX said in a statement. “If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket.”

SpaceX is streaming the flight from its X account and the company’s website. Coverage starts Friday at 5:15 p.m. ET, 30 minutes before the launch window opens.

The stream should continue through the launch and the Super Heavy V3 catch, expected approximately 6.5 minutes after launch. The company promises “hours of live views” of Starship as it orbits Earth, offering viewers excellent views of the planet from space.

SpaceX hasn’t specified if it’s going to stream the entire mission, including the second catch when Starship returns to Earth on Saturday, Nov. 14. The expected time of arrival for that landing is 4:17 p.m. ET, assuming no delays or technical problems, which is a little more than 22 hours after launch. SpaceX streams from the same places every time, so if the company does stream it, the links above will be where to go.

Should the launch be delayed due to weather, technical issues or something else (after all, it is Friday the 13th), SpaceX has not announced a backup launch date at this time.

Its funding model leans on customer prepayments and government grants rather than heavy upfront spending, a tension worth weighing as expansion plans take shape.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 4, 2026, GlobalFoundries (GFS -2.70%) reported record non-IFRS (financial metrics excluding non-cash items) gross margins of 31.4% from ramping differentiated technologies in high-growth applications. Data center demand for silicon photonics -- using light instead of electricity to transfer data -- isn't slowing down as artificial intelligence workloads scale. A landmark partnership for its Malta, New York site uses fee structures and cost reimbursements to generate wafer profits comparable to self-funded plants without heavy upfront capital expenditures, or capex, which are funds spent on physical equipment.

A deliberate pivot toward communications infrastructure, automotive chips, and internet of things (connected smart devices) hardware is insulating results from smartphone market volatility. Generating most sales outside mobile handsets helped the business deliver record gross margins while expanding average selling prices.

Optical networking demand and custom automotive chip adoption are accelerating across high-margin applications. GlobalFoundries relies on its flexible manufacturing footprint, proprietary silicon photonics, and government-backed funding structure to capture market share while tracking pricing discipline and mix optimization.

Expanding custom chip design wins positions the fab operator to capture higher value per wafer as edge computing and physical artificial intelligence scale.

The Soma Pro and Some Sense HD Haptics are part of an updated vibrating gaming chair lineup promising better immersion and improved comfort.

There are different levels of gaming immersion when it comes to haptics. On one side, you have controller haptics, which provide a bit of stimulation in games. There’s usually a nice little rumble from explosions or gunshots, and maybe a bit of vibration to give you some feedback while driving off-road.

On the other side, you have Razer’s two new gaming chairs, the $1,000 Soma Pro and the $570 Soma Sense HD Haptics, which feature some serious motors to really shake your spine. Both incorporate Razer Sensa HD Haptics, which the company first debuted as part of Project Esther back in 2024. There’s also THX Spatial Audio support and Razer Chroma RGB lighting built-in.

This isn’t an entirely new line for Razer. The Soma series is one the company has been working on for some years now. The Soma Chroma was the first wireless RGB gaming chair announced this summer for $499. Now Razer is rounding out its gaming chair lineup.

“The Soma Pro is where the chair finally joins the game,” said Addie Tan, Razer’s global head of its lifestyle division in a press statement. “For years, gamers have upgraded everything they see and hear, while the seat they spend every session in stayed on the sidelines. With Soma Pro, the chair becomes part of the game — you feel it, hear it and see it.”

Both chairs come with six haptic motor actuators built into each seat, unlike the $300 Razer Freyja, which was essentially a wired cushion you placed on top of your existing chair and plugged in. I actually owned the Freyja, and while it worked OK for some games, for a lot of others I tried it with, it just used a generic rumble without really customizing things. It was also very uncomfortable to sit on long-term, didn’t like the feeling of being tethered to a cable and ended up getting rid of it. A built-in wireless option, like these new chairs, seems like a much better solution to me.

Both new chairs deliver “multizone feedback” via Razer Sensa HD Haptics, and Razer says they should match the intensity, direction, and distance of in-game events. For example, an explosion off to the side will feel different from one that’s up close to you. So this isn’t just a generic rumble that applies to every situation; it’s customized based on the gameplay.

Razer lists more than 100 PC games that support integrated Sensa HD Haptics, including Battlefield 6, Borderlands 4, Marvel Rivals and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl. For everything else, the chairs use Audio-to-Haptics via Razer Synapse, converting audio into vibration, so the effect also works with games without native support, as well as with movies and music.

In theory, this should allow the feature to work on anything that supports controller vibration, but a Razer representative did not immediately respond to a request for clarification. On the Soma Pro, you can dial the overall intensity up or down in Synapse, or adjust each of the six motor zones individually.

It’s worth noting that, unlike the Freyja, both chairs are wireless, though that doesn’t mean they’re completely untethered since Razer hasn’t managed to break the laws of energy yet. Each chair draws power over a single USB-C connection, from either a wall outlet or a compatible power bank, to preserve what Razer calls a wireless-aesthetic setup. Neither a power bank nor a power adapter is included in the box, so budget for one if you want the cable-free look. That’s a downside because my LiberNovo Omni chair, which comes with adjustable lumbar support, a motorized spine, and even a massager setting, shipped with a rechargeable 2,200-mAh power bank.

Both chairs carry a three-year warranty on mechanisms and moving parts and a two-year warranty on electronic parts.

Both Soma chairs share the same hardware, at least where you rest your backside. There’s a built-in lumbar arch intended to encourage a neutral sitting position, a dual-density cold-cured foam seat cushion with a softer top layer over a firmer core, and a backrest that reclines up to 132 degrees. Both have a steel frame and are rated for people up to 331 pounds. Razer lists the Soma Pro for people 5 feet, 5 inches to 6 feet, 6 inches tall, and the Sensa model for 5 feet, 3 inches to 6 feet, 6 inches.

For $1,000, the Soma Pro offers sound and light in addition to haptics. Built-in speakers deliver THX Spatial Audio directly from the chair. Yes, that’s right: you don’t need computer speakers; they’re right behind your head now. You can use them on their own, or pair them with front speakers to widen the soundstage, with the chair effectively handling the rear of the setup. It is the same idea Razer has used with Razer Clio headrest speakers before, now integrated rather than clipped on.

The Pro is also the only model in the line with Razer Chroma RGB. The reactive lighting uses 16.8 million colors, responds to on-screen action in more than 300 integrated games, and syncs with the rest of a Razer setup via Synapse. While I love a good light show, this isn’t really meant for the person seated in the chair. It seems designed for streamers and people watching you, since it doesn’t look like you can really see the light show unless you take your eyes off the stream.

The Pro also gets the line’s most adjustable fit: 4D armrests, a magnetic head cushion and a frog tilt mechanism, on a powder-coated aluminum alloy wheelbase.

The controls are on a built-in panel that switches between Razer HyperSpeed Wireless (2.4 GHz) for PC and Bluetooth LE for mobile, with a companion Razer Furniture app on the Pro for adjusting haptics, audio and lighting from a phone. The controls are a nice alternative to using Razer’s annoyingly overlapping and often invasive Synapse and Chroma software.

The $570 Soma Sensa HD Haptics chair keeps the same six-actuator haptic system and drops the speakers and the RGB. That makes it $70 more than the lighting-only Soma Chroma ($499), and $430 less than the Soma Pro ($1,000). If you already have a headset or speakers, which I’d assume you do as a gamer who’s considering a product like this, the Soma Sensa HD Haptics gets you most of the key features without the unnecessary extras.
